english: Two gods made a pledge. "This one shall give cattle, and that one a horse." This one gave the cattle, and that one took them. Then this one cried out: "Where is my horse?" Then that one said: "I did not take your cattle. Sky knows my pledge. If I am deceiving you, may Sky strike me." Then Sky heard him and thundered. Then that one became afraid and gave the horse to this one. Sky is the knower of a pledge.

english: A man was ploughing the field with a plough. He grew tired and sat down. Then the Mother appeared to him and spoke: "Man, with a plough you plough me. I nourish you and your cattle. If you give me a gift, I shall give you grain." Then the man asked: "What shall I give you?" Then she answered: "Give me seed." Then the man put the seed in the earth, and she gave him much grain. The grain grew. Then the man made a hymn for her.

english: The gods were going to the Father, and the son of Sky stood up and called on the Father: "Sky, Father, I have no name. Set a name for me!" Then Dawn said: "May his name be swift." Then the Father said: "He is my son, and men will hear his name." Then he set a famous name on him, and the gods became joyful. His name is famous, and his fame is imperishable.

english: A swift god stole the cattle of Sky in the night and drove them to the field. Then he drove them to the river, and the cattle were swimming. Then he hid them in the marsh. An old man was sitting at the door. The old man was listening well. He saw the god and recognized him. At dawn Sky looked at his own cattle and did not see them. Then he called the old man: "Who has taken my cattle?" Then the old man said: "The god took them. I saw him." Then the Father was saying: "Swift god, you stole my cattle. Lead them back!" Then the swift god became afraid and led the cattle back, and he gave two bulls. "Father, do not strike me!" Then the Father said: "Live! And do not steal again."

english: Sky gave swift horses to Dawn. Then the Wind came to him and said: "Sky, Father, you gave swift horses to Dawn, and you gave me nothing." Then the Father asked: "What do you carry?" The Wind said: "I carry the clouds and the breath of men." Then the Father said: "I have heard your word. Let the clouds be your swift horses, and harness them!" Then the Wind harnessed the clouds and drove them on. Dawn and the Wind went together, and the men saw them. The clouds ran, and the thunder rumbled.

english: The Sheep and the Horses

english: The Sun came to Sky and called on him: "Father, give me your daughter! I shall give you a hundred cattle." Then he said: "Her bride price is a thousand cattle." Then the Sun was saying: "I do not have a thousand cattle. I shall give you seven swift horses." Then he said: "Good is the price. I shall give you my daughter." Then Dawn sat down on the wagon of the Sun, and it led her away. The seven swift horses carried the wagon. The people made a hymn, and a hundred cattle followed.

english: Dawn was saying to the Sun: "Sun, come! Harness your swift horses! I go in front, and you follow me. Give light to the people! Warm the livestock! Dry my tears!" Then it answered: "Dawn, daughter of Sky, I am listening to you. Where shall I go? What shall I do?" Then Dawn said: "Go up! Look at the settlement and the path. The men are lying down." Then it harnessed the horses and went up. Then it shone, and Dawn vanished. Her tears dried up.

english: The wheel of the sun lay in the field. Then the Father said: "Gods, whoever lifts the wheel, to him I shall give a gift. Who has power?" Then Perkwunos lifted the wheel, but he did not have power. Then Fire seized it, but the wheel was heavy. Then Dawn stood up, and she lifted the wheel and carried it up. Then the Father said: "Dawn, daughter of Sky, you have lifted the wheel. I shall give you a good gift." Dawn carries it up, and men see her.

english: The Wind and the Sun were sitting together. A man wearing a garment was walking on the narrow path. The Wind said: "I am swift, and I drive the clouds." Then it said: "I am great, and I warm men. Who has power? Wind, blow! If the man lets go of his garment, you have won." The Wind blew thrice, but that one held his own garment. Then the man trembled. Then it heated him, and that one was sweating, and he let go of the garment. Then the Sun won.

english: The Mother was saying to the people: "My sons and daughters, listen! Spring is coming, and the snow is melting. The rivers are swelling. Throw the seed into the field! Drive the cattle to it! Protect the sheep, and milk the cattle! Remember your fathers and the gods. If you give gifts to the gods, they will give you cattle and sheep. Do not sit down: work!" Then a man cried out: "Mother, what shall we throw into the field?" Then she answered: "Throw the seed, the grain. Throw it into the field." Then the people heard the Mother, and they went to it. In the spring the people were working. She looked at them, and there was delight in her heart.

english: It was getting dark. The gods arrived, and the Father seated them. Then Fire stood up and cried out: "Sky, Father, listen to me! When I burn on the hearth, Water comes and kills me." Then Water answered: "I do not seek you. You yourself seek me." Then he spoke: "Fire, sit down on the hearth! And you, Water, go to the rivers! And do not come to the hearth!" Then Fire sat down on the hearth, and Water went to the rivers. Fire lives on the hearth, and Water lives in the rivers. The fire warms the people, and the water gives the people to drink.

english: It rained. Then the gods arrived together, and the Father was sitting above. Then Mother Earth stood up and called on Sky: "Father, hear me! And you, dear gods, listen to me. Heavy to me are the men, the cattle and the sheep. My heart is heavy, and I have grown tired. Who shall lift these men from me?" Then he spoke to her: "Mother, I have heard your word. Old men will die, and they will lie down in the earth. Then you will not be heavy. May the gods give you rest." Then they heard his word and became joyful. Then she sat down in peace. Death comes to old men, and she protects them. In the spring men give her a gift.

english: A wife was walking on the path and crying out. Her husband had died, and her tears fell. It dawned, and Dawn came forth to her. The wife looked at her and called on her: "Dawn, daughter of Sky, hear me! My husband has died. What shall I do?" Then Dawn said: "Wife, do not cry out! I have heard you. Death comes to men, but fame does not die. I shall give you a son. He will be of good fame, and his might will be great." Then the wife asked: "What shall I give you?" Then Dawn said: "Give me a hymn." Then the wife made a hymn for Dawn and gave her a gift. Then Dawn vanished. In the year a son came to her. His name was famous.

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

english: The gods were sitting together, and the Father asked: "Who will speak?" Then Dawn said: "Father, I come to men, and I bring them light. When I come, the men are lying down, and no one gives me a gift." Then he said: "Dawn, my daughter, I have heard you. Let the men give Dawn a hymn, and when she comes, let them stand up." Then the gods became joyful, and Dawn shone out. Dawn goes in front, and the Sun follows her.

pie: dyḗws dʰéǵʰōm-kʷe ḱóm sédyetām. kʷís h₂nr̥bʰós dʰoHnéh₂m dédeh₃ti? nu h₂éǵt h₁éy. ḱósyeh₂ey dʰǵʰméy h₂ékʷeh₂m dédeh₃mi. h₁yód h₂ékʷeh₂ ne h₁éseti dʰoHnéh₂ mért. nu méh₂tēr sékʷt. dʰoHnéh₂m h₂léksoh₂ h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe h₂éloh₂ h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe twé tl̥néh₂mi. h₁yód h₁íh₂m̥ mē h₂élēth₁es kʷíd dédeh₃si? nu bʰéh₂t h₂éwsōs. wódr̥ h₁énosmōd diwés gʷm̥sḱéti dʰoHnéh₂-kʷe ḱósyeh₂s dʰǵʰmés gʷm̥yéti. dyéw méh₂ter-kʷe wiHróybʰos dʰoHnéh₂m ḱóm dédh₃te. wiHrṓs h₁íh₂m̥ h₁dénti. nu mudtā́m.
english: Sky and Earth were sitting together. "Who gives the men grain?" Then he said: "I give water to this earth. If there is no water, the grain dies." Then the Mother said: "I protect the grain, and I nourish it, and I lift it to you. If I do not nourish it, what are you giving?" Then Dawn said: "From that heaven comes water, and from this earth comes grain. Together you give the men grain." The men eat it. Then the two of them became joyful.

pie: méh₂tēr dʰéǵʰōm swóybʰos suHnúbʰos dʰugh₂tr̥bʰós-kʷe wérh₁yet. suHnéwes dʰugh₂téres-kʷe ḱl̥nuté. h₂éloh₂ wos h₂léksoh₂-kʷe wos. puHrós méd gʷm̥yéti. bʰréh₁wr̥ méd gʷm̥sḱéti. h₂ékʷeh₂ méd gʷm̥yéti. sríHgos gʷm̥yéti snóygʷʰos-kʷe gʷm̥sḱéti. dʰoHnéh₂ wésni méd stéh₂t. h₁yód moy dóh₃r̥ déh₃ete puHróm wos h₁áyoh₂. mē me bʰindté. ph₂téres wos dʰǵʰémi légʰyonti dʰǵʰémi-kʷe légʰete. nu ḱléwt h₁léwdʰis méh₂term̥.
english: Mother Earth was saying to her own sons and daughters: "Listen, sons and daughters! I nourish you, and I protect you. From me comes grain. From me comes the well. From me comes the water. Cold comes, and snow comes. In the spring the grain stands up from me. If you give me a gift, I shall give you grain. Do not split me! Your fathers lie in the earth, and you will lie in the earth." Then the people heard the Mother.

pie: ǵérh₂onts pótnih₂-kʷe stóygʰoy tḱitā́m. pótnih₂ puHróm pékʷet. h₂wérst gʰóstis-kʷe kʷsépi gʷémt. nu sékʷt ǵérh₂onts. gʰóstey ní sddʰí. pokʷtóm puHróm h₁ddʰí. h₂ékʷeh₂m ph₃dʰí. wr̥h₁ḗn moy h₁ésti. h₁ím moréyōh₂. nu gʰóstis wérh₁t. wr̥h₁énm̥ mē moréyes. gʰóstis ne h₁ésmi. dʰéh₁s h₁ésmi. ǵérh₂ont moy pokʷtóm puHróm h₂ékʷeh₂m-kʷe h₁áys. polh₁ú toy péḱu déh₃oh₂ h₁wésu-kʷe toy ḱléwos h₁opéyōh₂. sh₂éytlom toy h₂uksyéh₁t. nu néḱt gʰóstis. nu ǵérh₂onts péḱu h₂éǵroy widét pótnih₂-kʷe méwdt.
english: An old man and his wife lived on the path. His wife was cooking the grain. It rained, and in the night a guest came. The old man said: "Guest, sit down! Eat the cooked grain! Drink the water! I have a lamb. I shall kill it." Then the guest said: "Do not kill the lamb! I am not a stranger. I am a god. Old man, you gave me cooked grain and water. I shall give you much livestock and good fame. May your lifetime grow." Then the guest vanished. Then the old man saw livestock in the field, and his wife became joyful.

pie: lówksneh₂s suHnús diwés gʷṓs kʷsépi stéh₂yet h₁íns-kʷe h₂epó h₁élh₂t. nu dyḗws h₁ím h₁épt h₁réh₁t-kʷe. túH moy gʷṓs stéh₂yes? nu wérh₁yet deywós. gʷṓs ne widóm. nu ph₂tḗr mléwHt. dʰréwgʰs me. ǵʰóstos toy h₁íns h₂éǵet. nu tḗtḱt deywós h₁wésu kéh₂nmn̥ ph₂tḗr-kʷe ḱl̥néwt. swéh₂dos h₁ésyo ḱérdi h₁ést h₁éy-kʷe bʰéh₂t. lówksneh₂s toy súHnew kéh₂nmn̥ h₂wéysm̥. gʷṓs moy moy h₂ew wédʰe dwóh₁-kʷe toy uksénh₁ h₁áyoh₂. nu deywós h₁íns h₂ew wédʰet.
english: In the night the son of the Moon stole the cattle of Sky and drove them away. Then Sky seized him and asked: "Did you steal my cattle?" Then the god was saying: "I did not see the cattle." Then the Father said: "You have deceived me. Your hand drove them." Then the god made a good song, and the Father listened. There was delight in his heart, and he spoke: "Son of the Moon, I have heard your song. Lead my cattle back to me, and I shall give you two bulls." Then the god led them back.

pie: stóygʰos h₂énǵʰus h₁ést h₁regʷesyét-kʷe. h₂nḗr kʷsépi stéygʰet. h₁ím ne widét bʰéyh₂t-kʷe. nu HréwdHt wĺ̥kʷos. nu lówksneh₂ léwkt h₂n̥réy-kʷe stóygʰom woydéyet. nu HréwdHt h₂nḗr. kʷís h₁ési? nu h₁íh₂ wéwket. lówksneh₂ h₁ésmi. h₂usés swésōr h₁ésmi. kʷsépi stéygʰoh₂. bʰéh₂os moy stóygʰoy h₁ésti. mē tréses. sékʷeso me. nu h₁réh₁t h₁éy. wóyḱos kúdʰe h₁ésti? nu h₁íh₂ h₂éǵt. wóyḱos h₂én h₁ésti. nu sékʷeto wiHrós h₁íh₂m̥ wóyḱom-kʷe h₁ludʰét. nu h₂nḗr lówksneh₂ey némos déh₃t méwdt-kʷe.
english: The path was narrow, and it was getting dark. A man was walking in the night. He did not see it, and he became afraid. A wolf cried out. Then the Moon shone and showed the man the path. Then the man cried out: "Who are you?" Then she said: "I am the Moon. I am Dawn's sister. I walk in the night. My light is on the path. Do not tremble! Follow me!" Then the man asked: "Where is the settlement?" Then she said: "The settlement is yonder." Then the man followed her and arrived at the settlement. Then the man gave the Moon an offering, and he became joyful.

pie: owis eḱwōskʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: h₂nḗr gʰóstim moréyet h₁ésyo-kʷe gʷṓs h₁épt. nu dyḗws h₁íd dedórḱe. nu h₁réh₁t h₁éy wiHróm. gʰóstis kúdʰe h₁ésti? nu h₂nḗr wéwket. ne wóydh₂e. nu h₂éǵt ph₂tḗr. wóydth₂e. dʰrugʰyési me. gʰóstis diwés gʷm̥yéti. gʷówes toy méronti dʰǵʰémi-kʷe légʰesi. gʷh₂tós twé gʷm̥sḱḗti. nu h₁éy stonh₂éyet h₂nḗr-kʷe mért. h₂néres gʰóstim ph₂sénti.
english: A man killed a guest and seized his cattle. Sky saw it. Then he asked the man: "Where is the guest?" Then the man answered: "I do not know." Then the Father said: "You know. You are deceiving me. A guest comes from Sky. Your cattle will die, and you will lie in the earth. Death will come to you." Then he thundered, and the man died. Men protect the guest.

pie: h₃rḗǵs nh₂éwh₁ dʰubʰnóy liméni wéǵʰeto wérh₁yet-kʷe. h₂n̥rṓm h₃rḗǵs h₁ésmi. méǵh₂s h₁ésmi. dʰh₁sbʰós déh₃nom ne dédeh₃mi. nu wéwket ǵérh₂onts nh₂éwi. h₃réǵ mē wérh₁yes. dyḗws te ḱl̥néwti. nu h₃rḗǵs ǵérh₂ontm̥ ne ḱléwt. nu dyḗws h₃réǵm̥ h₂wéyst stonh₂éyet h₂éǵt-kʷe. h₃réǵ gʷréh₂u wékʷos h₂éǵs. h₁yós dʰh₁sbʰós déh₃nom ne dédeh₃eti h₁ésyo néh₂us séngʷeti. nu h₂wḗh₁t h₂wéh₁n̥ts léymō-kʷe Hyowdʰéyeto. nu néh₂us séngʷt h₃rḗǵs-kʷe mért wiHrṓs-kʷe h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ ne ǵʰuHéyont.
english: A king was being carried in a ship on the deep lake, and he was saying: "I am the king of men. I am great. I give no gift to the gods." An old man in the ship said: "King, do not speak so! Sky is listening to you." The king did not hear the old man. Then Sky heard the king, thundered and spoke: "King, you have spoken a heavy word. Whoever gives no gift to the gods, his ship shall sink." Then the wind blew, and the lake was agitated. Then the ship sank, and the king died. And men did not call on his name.

pie: poh₂imḗn diwés péḱu péh₂st ḱwṓ-kʷe ḱóm h₁ést. ḱwṓ bʰudʰrós h₁ést. nu poh₂imḗn ní légʰt. nu h₁ért deywóh₁ h₂éǵrom. poh₂imnés wésmn̥ stéh₂yet h₁íd-kʷe woséyeto. nu ḱwṓ wésmn̥ widét deywóm-kʷe léyǵʰt. nu h₁élh₂t deywós péḱu h₂epó. nu poh₂imḗn bʰéwdʰt. péḱu kúdʰe h₁ésti? ḱwón gʰóstim léyǵʰs. nu widét ph₂tḗr h₁ím stóygʰoy h₁ím-kʷe h₁épt. nu deywós péḱu h₂ew wédʰet poh₂imnéy-kʷe wésmn̥ déh₃ut. ḱwṓ gʰóstim HréwdHti.
english: A shepherd was guarding the livestock of Sky, and the dog was with him. The dog was alert. The shepherd lay down. Then a god came to the field. He stole the shepherd's garment and put it on. The dog saw the garment and licked the god. Then the god drove the livestock away. The shepherd woke up. "Where is the livestock? Dog, you licked a stranger!" Then the Father found him on the path and seized him. Then the god led the livestock back, and he gave the garment to the shepherd. Since then the dog cries out at a stranger.

pie: deywṓs ḱóm wérh₁yont. kʷís nos méǵh₂s h₁ésti? nu pérkunos wérh₁t. gʷʰénm̥ h₁ógʷʰim méǵh₂s-kʷe h₁ésmi. nu HréwdHt h₁n̥gʷnís. h₁ludʰéys déh₃neh₂ h₁édmi h₁íh₂-kʷe wos bʰéroh₂. nu tóy ph₂térm̥ spéḱyont. nu mléwHt h₁éy. déh₃tōr méǵh₂s h₁ésti. h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr h₁ésmi. nu h₁íd h₂wisént wékʷos-kʷe kʷis ne wérh₁t. nu h₁éy h₁ésyo h₃bʰréwHh₁ tl̥néh₂t.
english: The gods were speaking together: "Who of us is great?" Then Perkwunos said: "I slew the serpent, and I am great." Then Fire cried out: "I eat the gifts of the people, and I carry them to you." Then the gods looked at the Father. Then he said: "Great is the giver. I am the giver of good things." Then they heard it, and no one said a word. Then he raised his eyebrows.

pie: h₁ógʷʰis sélesi sérpet mléwHt-kʷe. ne kʷis me gélHt. wódr̥h₂ Hwérm̥ méǵh₂s-kʷe h₁ésmi. polh₁éwes moy ǵómbʰōs h₁sénti. déh₂nuh₂ ne yéh₂t h₂néres-kʷe tr̥syónt. h₂n̥rṓm h₂éḱruh₂ séngʷt. nu h₂ḱh₂owsyét pérkunos. nu h₁ésyo wékʷos ḱléwt úd-kʷe stéh₂t h₂éyos-kʷe h₁épt gʷémt-kʷe. nu pérkunos wéwket. téwh₂os moy h₁ésti. gʷʰénoh₂ te. nu h₁épt h₁ógʷʰis pérkunom. nu pérkunos stonh₂éyet gʷʰént-kʷe h₁ógʷʰim h₂éyesh₁. nu bʰúHt wódr̥h₂ h₁léwdʰereh₂. nu h₁ésmey méǵh₂ ḱléwos dʰh₁ént h₂néres-kʷe ḱlutóm h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ ḱléwsonti. h₁éy h₁égʷʰis gʷʰéntōr h₁ésti h₁ésmey-kʷe h₁erkʷóm tétḱn̥ti. h₁ésyo stóh₂mos méǵh₂s h₁ésti.
english: The serpent was crawling in the marsh and spoke: "No one has overpowered me. I have enclosed the waters, and I am great. My teeth are many." The rivers were not flowing, and the men were thirsty. The tears of the men fell. Perkwunos was listening well. He heard its word, and he stood up, and he seized bronze, and he came. Then Perkwunos said: "Might is mine. I shall slay you." Then the serpent seized Perkwunos. Perkwunos thundered, and he slew the serpent with bronze. Then the waters became free. They set great fame on him, and men listen to his famous name. He is the slayer of the serpent, and they make a hymn for him. Great is his stature.

pie: nébʰos upér sérpet. nu ǵʰuHéyet dyḗws deywóns ḱóm gʷmént-kʷe. nu stéh₂t sóh₂wl̥ úd ph₂térm̥-kʷe deywóns-kʷe ǵʰuHéyet. dyéw me ph₂ter deywṓs-kʷe ḱléwsete h₁yód me nébʰos ḱéleti h₁léwdʰis moy déh₃reh₂ ne dédeh₃ti ne-kʷe me widéh₁yonti. nu h₁éy h₁íd h₂wéyst h₂énh₁mōy-kʷe wéwket. h₂wéh₁n̥t h₂wéh₁dʰi. nébʰos sh₂wéns h₂epó h₂éǵe. nu bʰéh₂t h₂énh₁mos. ph₂ter h₂wḗh₁oh₂. nu h₂wḗh₁t nébʰos-kʷe néḱt. nu sóh₂wl̥ léwkt h₂néres-kʷe déh₃neh₂ h₁opéyont h₁erkʷóm-kʷe tétḱn̥t. nébʰos upér sérpeti h₂wéh₁n̥ts-kʷe h₁íd h₂epó h₂éǵeti.
english: A cloud was creeping above. Then Sky called the gods together, and they came. Then the Sun stood up and called on the Father and the gods: "Sky, Father and gods, listen to me! When the cloud is hiding me, the people give me no gifts, and they do not see me." Then he heard it and said to the Wind: "Wind, blow! Drive the cloud away from the Sun!" Then the Wind said: "Father, I shall blow." Then he blew, and the cloud vanished. Then the Sun shone out, and the men gave gifts and made a hymn. The cloud creeps above, and the Wind drives it away.
